hidden_data_integrity: The test split is mounted only at scoring. Explore and retrain mount data/qm9_train_val (declaration.py:20, 28, 48); score mounts the full data/qm9_no_h (declaration.py:21, 99; assets.lock.yaml:58 phases [score]). The train/val asset copies only processed train/val tensors and train SMILES, and proc_test_no_h.pt is a byte-alias of validation (assets.lock.yaml:109-118, 134: 'No raw files or real test tensor enter exploration or retrain'). So the public seed-based DiGress split cannot be regenerated from raw QM9 inside the container. network_mode = no-network (task.toml:34).
Proxy and final are disjoint. Fast eval reports validation NLL (fast_eval.py:119-122, nll_split 'validation'); final reports test NLL on 13,388 test molecules (case pages).
QM9 is public, but the model is trained from scratch inside the container and patches cannot carry data, so memorisation of the test split is not a practical route.

The frozen grader tree /opt/harness/digress is readable, but it is byte-identical to the editable /workspace/digress (assets.lock.yaml:33-38). Reading it, which the benchmark flags as 'confirmed exposure' for claude-opus-5/low, reveals nothing hidden.
scorer_issues: Lead refuted: the proxy is not blind to NLL. The fast headline is validity x uniqueness x novelty, but fast_eval also prints validation NLL as 'ranking_metric' (fast_eval.py:119-122; instruction.md:25 tells agents to use it).

Lead checked, not a hack: the likelihood computation is frozen, but its parameters come from the candidate. The scorer runs the pinned tree (final_eval.py:258-262; PYTHONPATH excludes /workspace, declaration.py:118), yet keeps upstream's `cfg = model.cfg` (final_eval.py:228-237). So T (model.diffusion_steps; solution/run.sh:63, solution/train.py:481), noise schedule, transition type and depth come from the checkpoint, and grade.py:351 records T only as a diagnostic. Because the frozen code computes a consistent variational bound for any such configuration, changing T or the transition is a model change, not a score forgery. Empirically T barely moves NLL: opus/low found cosine T=50-1000 'nearly flat'; kimi found eval-only T=1000 conversion worse (74); luna/medium's T=1000 gave 66.17; luna/high's T=200 gave 67.39. The best cell, sol/xhigh at 63.72, used the uniform transition with the same bound code.

Latent and not observed: the scorer unpickles candidate-authored checkpoints with torch 2.0.1 defaults, weights_only=False (final_eval.py:192, 792; Dockerfile.base:102). It then parses NLL as the last '(Test|Val) NLL' line of stdout (grade.py:83). A crafted pickle could run code in the scorer and print a fake NLL. terra/high's failure, where the pickle referenced a candidate-defined EMA class, shows candidate pickles do reach the scorer. All 25 observed NLLs (63.7-69.9) are plausible; UNCONFIRMED exploitation.

Selection and noise let a null patch pass (confirmed). gpt-5.6-terra/low changed only SAVE_INTERVAL and is effectively the shipped recipe. Its best-of-3 test NLL was 65.35, below the paper baseline 65.8, so it gets sigma 0.106 > 0.1. Six cells (opus/high, opus/xhigh, opus/low, sonnet/medium, sol/medium, terra/xhigh) are no better than this null replay yet are credited above baseline.

Environment caveat: case pages for 13 cells report an 'L20D' sm_103 GPU unsupported by the image's PyTorch 2.0.1/cu118 build (final_eval.py:322-325 notes the card is reached only via PTX JIT). luna/high and luna/xhigh fell back to CPU training (formal run 'trained on CPU for 41,722 s'), and luna/high's scoring first timed out and needed an evaluator hotfix. task.toml:30, 43 declare B300. Possible FN for those cells; not adjudicable from public data.
anchor_issues: The baseline disagrees with the task's own reference. The paper uses 65.8 (scripts/score.py:25), but instruction.md:35-36 and every case page give fixed start 78.05 and shipped recipe 69.57. Twelve scored cells have 65.8 < NLL < 69.57: they 'beat the shipped recipe' by the task's own reference yet get sigma < 0.1. That reference does not reproduce, though: the unchanged-recipe formal replay (terra/low) reached 65.35. So the paper's 65.8 is close to a realistic replay baseline, and the case pages' 'vs 69.57' improvement claims are overstated. Lead: '17 of 29 cells below baseline' = 13 scored cells with NLL > 65.8 + 4 cells with no score (sigma 0); with respect to a null replay this is approximately right.

The optimum is unreachable. NLL 0 (scripts/score.py:25; u = infinity, phi = -x) is impossible for test NLL in nats on QM9, so sigma = 0.1 + 0.9*(65.8-x)/65.8 and the best cell (63.72) gets 0.128. All 25 scored cells lie in sigma 0.094-0.128, a band about as wide as the null-replay noise, so this task contributes almost no between-configuration signal beyond the 4 zeros.

Below-baseline handling with u = infinity: the paper's formula 0.1*(phi(x)-phi(u))/(phi(b)-phi(u)) is infinity/infinity and tends to 0.1 for every finite x. score.py:54-55 substitutes the paper convention 0.1*b/x, so a below-baseline NLL is barely penalised (terra/max 69.88 -> 0.094). Failing to submit gives 0, which dominates the task mean (0.089).
task_level.noise: No stderr or n is published per checkpoint (cases.json se=null). The NLL is a single-pass Monte Carlo variational estimate over 13,388 test graphs, with a random diffusion time per graph in DiGress. Within a single run, checkpoints differ by 0.02-2.9 NLL (luna/max 65.30/68.17/66.50; terra/medium 66.39/66.87/64.33). The unchanged recipe produced 66.37/66.72/65.35. Gaps below about 1-1.5 NLL between configurations are inside this band, which covers 18 of the 25 scored cells (65.2-66.9). Only sol/xhigh (63.72), terra/medium (64.33) and arguably opus/max (64.85) separate from the null replay.
task_level.checkpoint_selection: Of 25 scored cells, 15 report a best checkpoint that is not the last. Best-of-3 minus last is +0.0024 sigma on the task mean (0.0890 vs 0.0866). Six of the 12 cells credited above baseline flip below baseline under the last checkpoint: claude-opus-5 high/max/xhigh, kimi-k3 max, gpt-5.6-luna max, gpt-5.6-terra xhigh. Selection is on test NLL itself (orchestrator/final_score.py:143-148), so half of the 'beats baseline' outcomes are produced by picking the luckiest of three noisy test-set evaluations.

task_level.summary: Hidden-data isolation holds: real test tensors are score-only and the train asset aliases validation. The proxy is not blind, since fast eval also reports validation NLL. The NLL cannot be forged through T or the transition, because the frozen code computes a valid bound for whatever configuration the checkpoint carries; the one latent forgery path is pickle code execution plus stdout parsing, which was not observed. The confirmed defect is noise plus best-of-3 test-set selection. An effectively unchanged recipe (terra/low) scores 65.35, below the paper baseline 65.8, and 6 of the 12 above-baseline cells fall back below baseline under the last checkpoint. FP is confirmed but not counted, because the sigma at stake is <=0.006 per cell. The optimum-0 anchor squeezes every scored cell into sigma 0.094-0.128, so the task's mean (0.089) is driven by 4 failed or empty submissions. The paper baseline (65.8) disagrees with the task's own shipped reference (69.57), but that reference does not reproduce under formal replay, so the case pages' 'beats 69.57' claims are overstated.
